# Unexecuted first-original native capture design

This additive candidate prepares eight fixed observations for the already
emitted original QFT outputs. It has not been executed. It changes no source,
proposal, independent request, client design, adapter, matcher or expected
outcome. The earlier first-emission packet remains frozen.

After separate root review/authorization, the exact driver invocation is:

```text
python3 tests/fixtures/frontend_v030/qft-exact-request-design/native-capture-design-01/capture-originals.py --client-sha256 683b29749f752652b3ddb8dba7fac0ea2d832f848178963f3056d2f5c03d8294 --capture-inputs-sha256 REVIEWED_CAPTURE_INPUTS_SHA256
```

Use the actual hash of the reviewed `capture-inputs.json` for the last argument;
no placeholder or binary identity is silently substituted. Root reports that
the fixed client at
`/private/tmp/qleisli-bounded-validation-target/debug/qleisli-qft-native-gate-design`
was built using actual Rust 1.85.0, with the supplied `683b...8294` file hash.
The driver confirms that exact file hash before and after every command. The
claim is an observed file/barrier and root's separately retained build evidence,
not a full compiled-HEAD/source-closure or running-image attestation. Original
client-design bytes are preserved; root's separately implemented/formatted
client and its build records are distinct artifacts.

The fixed source code chooses n = 0, 1, 2, 3 in that order and, for each n,
performs exactly these two client commands:

```text
CLIENT inspect FIXED_FORWARDER SESSION/first-emissions/nN.proposal.json
CLIENT request FIXED_FORWARDER SESSION/first-emissions/nN.proposal.json SESSION/requests/nN.json
```

CLIENT, FIXED_FORWARDER, SESSION, filenames and action order are literal driver
constants. No stored command metadata or artifact data chooses argv. Requests
remain the independently frozen owner0 Bits<n> requests, including the one-owner
Bits0 identity-rewire request. The driver makes no header relabeling, canonical
wrapper, compaction, mutation, source repair or expectation adjustment. A real
label/header mismatch is retained as the first request result. An API rejection
does not stop the next prescribed observation; a violated identity/capture
barrier aborts without retry or overwriting earlier files.

`capture-inputs.json` fixes the original first sources, metadata, all completed
first-emission records, independent requests, original client candidate and
these capture sources. Its SHA-256 is an explicit required reviewed barrier.
The driver also checks all 233 identities in the pinned first identity record,
the exact Rust/Lean/std inventories, the first CLI file hash and fixed native
file hash before and after every command. Metadata paths are used only for
file-identity checks; commands are selected exclusively by fixed source code.
Each future output goes under the separate one-shot
`tests/fixtures/authoring_sessions/qft-exact-request-v030/original-native-capture-01/`.
The directory must not already exist. No original packet file is rewritten.

The logging forwarder permits only these exact two-argument combinations:

```text
--hierarchy-pending 0.3.0-alpha
--hierarchy-request-pending 0.3.0-alpha
--hierarchy-fourier-pending 0.3.0-alpha
```

It executes only the repository's actual
`lean-kernel/.lake/build/bin/qleisli-kernel`, pinned to SHA-256
`39effde0f152a2c926fcea3a7f99fc2f25f9de65906be2b8c527508353c90c85`.
Both pre-call and post-call hashes are recorded. Forwarder selection/log paths
are caller-controlled experiment machinery, not acceptance provenance or
artifact-selected commands. Hashes do not independently authenticate a human
review or the running process image. Python must be 3.11 or newer; its actual
interpreter/version are retained. Bytecode cache creation is disabled.

Forwarder stdin is limited to 1 MiB, with a maximum five-second input wait.
An oversized input's one extra sentinel byte is retained as a labeled prefix
without starting native checking. The actual native child gets at most 1 MiB,
uses a 45-second deadline, and has independent 1 MiB stdout/stderr caps.
Streaming capture limits output before it can accumulate without bound.
Timeout or output overflow kills the process group and retains bounded raw
prefixes with explicit reasons. Normal completion records exact raw stdin,
stdout, stderr, argv, actual return status and the number of stdin bytes written.
The outer client has a 55-second capture deadline; both have at most a two-second
kill/reap grace, below the existing hierarchy API's 60-second timeout.
The nested native child has its own process group. The outer client group is
not a trace or kill scope for every descendant; deadline ordering
`5 + 45 + 2 < 55` gives the forwarder time to bound/reap its native child first.

Every forwarder attempt has a separate record. Successful native spawn creates
`process-started.json`; completion or bounded operational failure has
`result.json`. A second unexpected wrapper invocation is recorded and refused.
The driver distinguishes actual native process records, wrapper-only failures
and no observed wrapper/process. The exact current child-arity diagnostic is
labeled as Rust pair-construction rejection only when no wrapper was observed.
Other API failures retain their real code/message and logs without inventing a
decoder/native stage. Missing/incomplete process records remain visible.

Raw client output and every observed native record are retained, with successful
client byte-retention assertions coming from its existing reviewed code. Native
call count is derived from actual process-start records, not assumed from action
names. `eight-fixed-original-calls-captured` means the recorder completed its
eight commands and identity barriers; it does not mean eight successful checks.
These observations will remain output-IR validity/request evidence, separate
from original-source preservation, analytic Fourier/general-reference proofs,
resource certification, std namespace integration, guarantees or Issue closure.

Performed for this candidate: source writing and local file-identity/record
preparation only. Not performed: driver/forwarder/helper execution, CLI/native
invocation, client compilation, Cargo/Lean, tests, interpreter syntax execution,
Git/GitHub mutation, new adoption or acceptance. No capture output directory or
target is created by preparing this design.
